mainTopic: The end of the אגדה on the חכמים's prayer and the "אבירי לב"; the חתן and יוהרא contradiction; and the opening of פרק מי שמתו on the mourner before burial.
overview: The גמרא finishes a prayer of the חכמים from תהלים, reading each phrase as a request that no traitor like אחיתופל, דואג or גחזי, and no one who sins in public, come out of their circle. Next it brings a מחלוקת about the "אבירי לב" of ישעיהו. One view says the צדיקים earn their food by right. The other says the world is fed in their merit while they barely eat, as the בת קול about רבי חנינא בן דוסא shows. רב יהודה reads the phrase as describing stubborn people who never convert, and רב יוסף and רב אשי back him up. The גמרא then returns to the משנה about a חתן saying שמע and asks why רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and the רבנן seem to switch their views on showing off in the case of working on תשעה באב. רבי יוחנן answers by swapping the names, and רב שישא shows that each side is consistent as it stands. The chapter היה קורא ends, and פרק מי שמתו begins with the rule that a mourner whose dead is not yet buried is exempt from מצוות, along with rules for pallbearers, comforters, and women, slaves and minors. The גמרא infers that the exemption applies only when the body is before him, and challenges this with a ברייתא about a mourner eating in another room. The discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: No traitor should come out of our group
steps.stepSummary: The first three phrases of the פסוק are read as prayers that no traitor like אחיתופל, דואג האדומי or גחזי come out of the חכמים's circle.
steps.simpleTranslation: "There is no breach": may our group not be like דוד's group, from which אחיתופל came out. "And no going forth": may our group not be like שאול's group, from which דואג האדומי came out. "And no outcry": may our group not be like אלישע's group, from which גחזי came out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is continuing its explanation of a prayer, reading each phrase of the פסוק as a request about the people in our group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each phrase is tied to a great leader whose close circle produced someone who went bad: אחיתופל betrayed דוד, דואג informed for שאול, and גחזי failed אלישע. The prayer asks that our own group stay loyal and whole.

keyTerms.meaning: A breach or crack, a break in the wall
A group or circle of people
Going out, here meaning someone who leaves for a bad path

phrases.english: "There is no breach":
phrases.notes: These words come from תהלים 144:14, which the חכמים used as a prayer.

phrases.english: that our group should not be
like the group of David,
from which Achitophel came out.
"And no going forth":
that our group should not be
like the group of Saul,
from which Doeg the Edomite came out.
"And no outcry":
that our group should not be
like the group of Elisha,
from which Geichazi came out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the explanation of the חכמים's prayer from the earlier part of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The phrases אין פרץ, אין יוצאת and אין צוחה are prayers that no traitor come out of our group, unlike the groups of דוד, שאול and אלישע.

steps.title: No child or student who sins in public
steps.stepSummary: The last word, "ברחובותינו", is read as a prayer that we not have a child or student who sins publicly, like ישו הנוצרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: "In our open places": may we not have a son or student who burns his food in public, like ישו הנוצרי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the prayer by explaining the last word of the פסוק, "in our streets".
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Streets" means in public, so this asks that no one from our home or yeshiva shame us openly. "Burning his food" is a picture of ruining himself in front of everyone and pulling others down with him.

keyTerms.meaning: Streets or open squares, meaning in public
Burns his cooked food, a picture for sinning or ruining himself
In public, in front of many people

steps.whatToRemember: The whole prayer asks for one thing: that our circle of family and students stay loyal and not produce someone who betrays or shames it.

phrases.english: "In our open places":
that we should not have
a son or a student
who burns his food in public,
phrases.notes: This isn't about cooking. It's a picture of someone who goes bad publicly and ruins things for others.

phrases.english: such as Yeshu the Notzri.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּרְחוֹבוֹתֵינוּ שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא לָנוּ בֵּן אוֹ תַּלְמִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the final word of the same פסוק, closing the explanation of the prayer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: "ברחובותינו" is a prayer not to have a son or student who sins in public.

steps.title: Who are the stubborn-hearted? First opinion
steps.stepSummary: A new פסוק is brought, with a מחלוקת between רב and שמואל (or רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר). The first opinion says the world is fed as charity, but the צדיקים earn their food by right.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Listen to Me, you stubborn-hearted, who are far from צדקה": רב and שמואל disagree, and some say it was רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר. One said: the whole world is fed through charity, but they are fed by force.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic, another פסוק whose meaning is argued about by the same pairs of אמוראים, and gives the first opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides read the "stubborn-hearted" as צדיקים who are strong in serving ה׳. The first opinion says the rest of the world gets food as a gift (צדקה), but the צדיקים are "far from צדקה" because their good deeds give them a right to it, like taking it by strength.

keyTerms.meaning: By force, literally by the arm, meaning by right

steps.confusionAlert: "Far from צדקה" here does not mean they don't give charity! It means they don't need ה׳'s charity, because they earned what they get.

phrases.english: "Listen to Me, you stubborn-hearted,
who are far from charity":
Rav and Shmuel,
and some say
Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Elazar, argued about it.
One said:
the whole world is fed through charity,
but they are fed by force.
phrases.notes: "They" are the צדיקים. Their own good deeds give them the right to their food.

steps.triggerLanguage: שִׁמְעוּ אֵלַי אַבִּירֵי לֵב הָרְחוֹקִים מִצְּדָקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new פסוק explanation, linked to the earlier one because the same disputants are uncertain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to one view, the world is fed as a gift, while the צדיקים are fed by the right they earned.

steps.title: Second opinion: the world eats in their merit
steps.stepSummary: The second opinion says the whole world is fed in the merit of the צדיקים, while they themselves do not get fed even through their own merit. The גמרא points to רב יהודה's teaching as support.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one said: the whole world is fed in their merit, but they are not fed even in their own merit, like what רב יהודה said in the name of רב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second opinion and says it fits a teaching of רב יהודה in the name of רב, which it will bring next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here "far from צדקה" means the צדיקים get almost nothing for themselves, even though everyone else is fed thanks to them. The words "like רב יהודה" set up the next step, which shows this idea in action.

keyTerms.meaning: In their merit, because of them
In their own merit, for themselves
Like the teaching of רב יהודה

phrases.english: And one said:
the whole world is fed in their merit,

phrases.aramaic: וְהֵם אֲפִילּוּ בִּזְכוּת עַצְמָן אֵין נִזּוֹנִין.
phrases.english: but they are not fed even in their own merit.
This is like what Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחַד אָמַר כָּל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ נִזּוֹנִין בִּזְכוּתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing side of the מחלוקת begun in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the second view, the world is fed through the צדיקים' merit while they themselves receive almost nothing.

steps.title: The heavenly voice about רבי חנינא בן דוסא
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב: every day a בת קול says the whole world is fed because of חנינא, yet a קב of carobs is enough for him all week.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יהודה said in the name of רב: every day a בת קול goes out from הר חורב and says, "The whole world is fed because of חנינא My son, and for חנינא My son a קב of carobs is enough from one ערב שבת to the next ערב שבת."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the teaching it pointed to, which shows the second opinion is true.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בת קול says both parts of the second opinion: the world eats because of רבי חנינא בן דוסא, and he himself lives on a tiny amount of carobs for a whole week. That is exactly "the world is fed in their merit, but they are not fed in their own merit".

keyTerms.meaning: A קב (a small measure) of carobs, a cheap, plain food

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the famous source for how poorly רבי חנינא בן דוסא lived even though the whole world was supported in his merit.

phrases.english: As Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
Every single day a heavenly voice
goes out from Mount Chorev and says:
The whole world is fed
because of Chanina My son,
phrases.notes: This is רבי חנינא בן דוסא.

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲנִינָא בְּנִי דַּי לוֹ בְּקַב חָרוּבִין
phrases.english: and for Chanina My son a kav of carobs is enough
from one Shabbat eve to the next Shabbat eve.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב בְּכָל יוֹם וְיוֹם בַּת קוֹל יוֹצֵאת מֵהַר חוֹרֵב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the teaching referenced by "כדרב יהודה אמר רב" as support for the second opinion.
steps.raayaObject: The second opinion: the world is fed in the צדיקים' merit while they themselves are not.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The daily בת קול about רבי חנינא בן דוסא, quoted by רב יהודה in the name of רב.

steps.title: רב יהודה reads the פסוק differently
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that both opinions argue with רב יהודה, who says the "אבירי לב" are the foolish people of גובאי, not צדיקים at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this argues with רב יהודה, for רב יהודה said: who are the "stubborn-hearted"? The foolish people of גובאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רב יהודה has his own reading of the same פסוק, which clashes with the ones just given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, everyone read "אבירי לב" as praise for צדיקים. רב יהודה reads it as an insult: stubborn, foolish non-Jews who are truly far from goodness.

keyTerms.meaning: The people of גובאי, a non-Jewish nation

steps.confusionAlert: It is the same רב יהודה who just quoted the בת קול about רבי חנינא. That was in the name of רב; here רב יהודה gives his own, different reading of the פסוק.

phrases.english: And this argues with Rav Yehuda.
For Rav Yehuda said:
Who are the "stubborn-hearted"?
The foolish people of Gova.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the reading of the פסוק in steps 3 to 5 is not the only one; רב יהודה disagrees.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב יהודה, "אבירי לב" are the foolish people of גובאי.

steps.title: רב יוסף's proof: none of them ever converted
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף backs up רב יהודה: you can see they are stubborn, because no convert ever came from them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Know that this is so, because not one convert has ever converted from them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף brings a proof that רב יהודה's reading is right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being "stubborn-hearted" and "far from צדקה" fits a people so closed off that not one of them ever joined the Jewish people. That real-life fact supports reading the פסוק as being about גובאי.

keyTerms.meaning: Know (that this is true), used to bring a proof

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to read "אבירי לב": as צדיקים (in two versions, ending with the בת קול about רבי חנינא), or, according to רב יהודה, as the foolish people of גובאי, from whom no one ever converted.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: Know that this is so,
for not one convert has ever converted from them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב יהודה's reading given in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: רב יהודה's view that "אבירי לב" are the people of גובאי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The fact that no one from גובאי ever converted, showing how stubborn they are.

steps.title: רב אשי: the people of מתא מחסיא are the stubborn-hearted
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the people of מתא מחסיא are the 'אבירי לב', because they see the glory of Torah twice a year and still none of them convert.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The people of the town מתא מחסיא are the 'stubborn of heart.' They see the honor of the Torah twice a year, and still not one convert comes from them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives another example of 'אבירי לב', using the same reasoning רב יוסף just used about the people of גובאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף proved that the people of גובאי are stubborn because no convert ever came from them. רב אשי applies the same test to his own town, and his case is even stronger. These people see Torah honored in public twice every year and are still not moved.

keyTerms.meaning: The town of מחסיא, where רב אשי lived and taught
The honor or glory of the Torah

steps.whatToRemember: In רב יהודה's reading, 'אבירי לב' are stubborn people who see the truth and do not respond. רב יוסף brings a proof for this from גובאי, and רב אשי adds the people of מתא מחסיא. This is one side of the disagreement; the other side reads the פסוק as being about צדיקים.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
The people of the town of Mechasya
are the "stubborn of heart,"
phrases.notes: This is the same phrase from the פסוק that the גמרא has been explaining, ישעיהו 46:12.

phrases.english: for they see the glory of the Torah
twice a year,
phrases.notes: This means the two big yearly gatherings, when crowds came to his town to learn Torah together.

phrases.english: and not a single convert converts from among them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: בְּנֵי מָתָא מַחְסֵיָא ״אַבִּירֵי לֵב״ נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a parallel example using the same reasoning as רב יוסף's support for רב יהודה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The people of מתא מחסיא are 'אבירי לב', since they see Torah's glory and never convert.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: a groom who wants to recite שמע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the start of the משנה about a חתן who wishes to say קריאת שמע on his wedding night.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'A groom, if he wants to read [קריאת שמע], etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes the line about a groom who wants to say שמע. This sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה rules that a חתן is excused from קריאת שמע on his wedding night, but he may say it if he wants to. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagrees, because he worries the groom is acting more pious than others (יוהרא). The גמרא is now about to look closely at this argument.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Etc.' The quote continues in the משנה

phrases.english: A groom, if he wants
to recite, etc.
phrases.notes: The rest of the משנה says he may, but רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says not everyone who wants to take on a pious reputation may do so.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the אגדה and returns to the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The רבנן say a groom may choose to say שמע. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says he should not, because it looks like showing off.

steps.title: Are the opinions on showing off reversed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: does this mean רבן שמעון בן גמליאל worries about showing off and the רבנן do not? We have heard them say the opposite!
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל worries about showing off, and the רבנן do not worry about showing off? But we have heard them say the opposite!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges how the argument in the משנה lines up. Elsewhere, each side seems to hold the reverse view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the groom's case, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is the one worried about יוהרא, and the רבנן are not. The גמרא says it knows of another place where the positions are flipped. If so, each side seems to contradict itself.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Is that to say…?' The גמרא checks what follows from a statement
Showing off, acting more pious than others

phrases.english: Is that to say

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל חָיֵישׁ לְיוּהֲרָא
phrases.english: that Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel is concerned about showing off
and the Rabbis are not concerned about showing off?
But we have heard them say the opposite!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל חָיֵישׁ לְיוּהֲרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the positions in the משנה just quoted
steps.kashyaTarget: The positions of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and the רבנן in the חתן משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Their views about יוהרא here seem to be the reverse of their views in another משנה.

steps.title: The source: working on תשעה באב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about working on תשעה באב. The רבנן say only Torah scholars hold back from work everywhere. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says anyone may act like a Torah scholar.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: In a place where people usually work on תשעה באב, they work. In a place where people usually do not work, they do not work. Everywhere, Torah scholars do not work. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: A person may always act like a Torah scholar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the משנה that shows the 'opposite' positions it just mentioned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the רבנן say only real Torah scholars may refrain from work everywhere. This implies that an ordinary person who refrains would be showing off, so the רבנן do worry about יוהרא. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל lets anyone act like a scholar, so he does not worry about it.

keyTerms.meaning: The fast of the Ninth of Av
Hold back from work, are idle

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:

phrases.aramaic: מָקוֹם שֶׁנָּהֲגוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת מְלָאכָה בְּתִשְׁעָה בְּאָב
phrases.english: A place where they were accustomed to do work on the Ninth of Av
they may work.
A place where they were accustomed not to work
they may not work.
And in every place, Torah scholars refrain from work.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
A person may always make
himself like a Torah scholar.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: מָקוֹם שֶׁנָּהֲגוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת מְלָאכָה בְּתִשְׁעָה בְּאָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source behind the challenge
steps.raayaObject: That the רבנן worry about יוהרא and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל does not
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about working on תשעה באב

steps.title: A double contradiction
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sums up the problem. The רבנן contradict themselves, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל contradicts himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן contradict the רבנן, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל contradicts רבן שמעון בן גמליאל!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the challenge in its full form: each side says one thing about the groom and the opposite about תשעה באב. The next steps answer it: רבי יוחנן in step 13, and רב שישא in steps 14 and 15.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the groom, the רבנן do not worry about showing off. With תשעה באב, they do. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is the reverse: he worries about it with the groom but not with תשעה באב.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not one side against the other. Each side contradicts its OWN view from the other משנה, which is why the line says the same name twice.

phrases.english: There is a contradiction between the Rabbis and the Rabbis,
there is a contradiction between Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel
and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel!

steps.triggerLanguage: קַשְׁיָא דְּרַבָּנַן אַדְּרַבָּנַן, קַשְׁיָא דְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אַדְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: States the contradiction in full, using the source just quoted
steps.kashyaTarget: How each side can be consistent between the חתן case and the תשעה באב case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each side's concern about יוהרא flips between the two משניות.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן switches the names
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers the contradiction by saying that the names in one of the two משניות are switched.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: the opinions are switched.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the first answer to the double contradiction. He says that in one of the two משניות, the names of who holds what should be swapped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the names are swapped, each side is consistent. The same תנא worries about showing off in both cases, and the other side doesn't worry in either case. This answer changes the text of the source and does not explain any difference between the cases.

keyTerms.meaning: The opinions are switched. The names attached to each view should be reversed.
The חכמים, meaning the majority opinion in the משנה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
The opinions are switched.
phrases.notes: He means: swap the names in one of the two משניות, so each תנא says the same thing in both places.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the double contradiction raised in Step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the text: the names of the תנאים are reversed in one source.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each תנא seemed to hold opposite views in the two משניות.
steps.terutzMaskana: After the names are swapped, each תנא is consistent in both places.

steps.title: No switch needed: the רבנן are consistent
steps.stepSummary: רב שישא says not to switch the names. Reading שמע is something everyone does, so it does not stand out. Not working while everyone else works does stand out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שישא son of רב אידי said: Really, don't switch. The רבנן against the רבנן is no problem. With קריאת שמע, everyone is saying it and he is saying it too, so it doesn't look like showing off. Here, everyone is working and he is not, so it looks like showing off.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שישא gives a second answer that keeps the names as they are. First he shows that the רבנן do not contradict themselves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Showing off depends on whether a person stands out from everyone else. A חתן saying שמע is doing what everyone does, so the רבנן let him. A person refusing to work on תשעה באב while everyone else works does stand out, so the רבנן don't let him.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, don't switch. Keep the text as it is.
It is not difficult. There is no real contradiction.
Showing off, acting as if you are more pious than others.

phrases.aramaic: רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rav Sheisha son of Rav Idi said:
Really, do not switch.
The Rabbis against the Rabbis is no problem:
With reciting Shema,
since everyone is reciting it
and he is also reciting it,
it does not look like showing off.

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא, כֵּיוָן דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא עָבְדִי מְלָאכָה
phrases.english: Here, since everyone is doing work
phrases.notes: "Here" means the case of תשעה באב.

phrases.english: and he is not working,
it looks like showing off.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם לֹא תַּחְלִיף. דְּרַבָּנַן אַדְּרַבָּנַן לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer from רבי יוחנן's. It keeps the text and finds a difference between the cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (חילוק): standing out compared with blending in.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן seemed to allow showing off in one case and forbid it in the other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Showing off only applies when you act differently from everyone else. Saying שמע blends in, but not working stands out.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is consistent too
steps.stepSummary: With קריאת שמע, the issue is concentration, and everyone knows a חתן can't concentrate. On תשעה באב, people will just assume he has no work.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל against רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is no problem. There, it depends on concentration, and we can all see he can't focus his mind. But here, someone who sees him will say, "He just has no work." Go out and see how many idle people are in the market!
steps.whatsHappening: רב שישא continues his answer and shows that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל does not contradict himself either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the חתן, קריאת שמע needs concentration, and it is obvious he can't concentrate on his wedding night. So when he says it anyway, he is claiming a focus everyone knows he lacks, and that is showing off. On תשעה באב, people just think he is out of work, since plenty of people sit idle anyway, so nothing stands out.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally, "we are witnesses." It is obvious to everyone.
The person who sees him, an onlooker.

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides stay consistent once you look at how things appear to onlookers. The רבנן ask whether he stands out from the crowd. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל asks whether he is claiming something everyone knows isn't true.

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אַדְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל לָא קַשְׁיָא:
phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel against Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel is no problem:
There, the matter depends on concentration,
phrases.notes: "There" means the חתן saying שמע on his wedding night.

phrases.english: and we can all testify
that he cannot focus his mind.
But here, one who sees him says:
He simply has no work.
Go out and see
how many idle people there are in the market.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אַדְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רב שישא's answer by solving the second half of the contradiction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (חילוק): a claim that is obviously untrue compared with behavior that looks ordinary.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל seemed to worry about showing off with the חתן but not on תשעה באב.
steps.terutzMaskana: With the חתן, everyone knows he can't concentrate, so saying שמע looks like showing off. Idleness on תשעה באב looks normal.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק היה קורא
steps.stepSummary: The second chapter of ברכות, היה קורא, ends here.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter "היה קורא."
steps.whatsHappening: This is the traditional line said when finishing a chapter. It closes פרק היה קורא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is argued here. It marks a break, so the next line begins a new chapter with a new topic.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you. Said at the end of a chapter.
The name of the second chapter of ברכות.

phrases.english: We will return to you,
"Hayah Korei" (the chapter name).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the last discussion.

steps.title: A mourner before burial is exempt from מצוות
steps.stepSummary: The new chapter opens: someone whose dead relative is still lying before him, not yet buried, is exempt from קריאת שמע, תפלה, תפילין, and all the מצוות of the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone whose dead is lying before him is exempt from קריאת שמע, from תפלה, from תפילין, and from all the מצוות stated in the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter, פרק מי שמתו, begins with a new משנה. It teaches that a person whose relative died and has not been buried yet does not have to do these מצוות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list starts with the same מצוות the earlier chapters discussed, קריאת שמע and תפלה. Then it widens to every מצוה in the Torah. The משנה gives the rule without giving a reason here.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה. Written in short as מַתְנִי׳.
His dead, meaning his relative who died.
Lying before him, not yet buried.

steps.confusionAlert: פָּטוּר means he does not have to do these מצוות while the dead is unburied. It does not mean these מצוות stop applying to him for good.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the main source for the הלכה of אונן, the mourner before burial.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: One whose dead lies before him
phrases.notes: "His dead" means a relative of his who died and has not been buried yet.

phrases.english: is exempt from reciting Shema
and from prayer and from tefillin,
and from all the מצוות stated in the Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new chapter with a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person whose dead relative is still unburied is exempt from קריאת שמע, תפלה, תפילין, and all the מצוות of the Torah.

steps.title: Pallbearers: who is exempt and who is not
steps.stepSummary: Pallbearers who have not yet carried are exempt from קריאת שמע. Those who already carried are obligated. Both groups are exempt from תפלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The pallbearers, their replacements, and the replacements of their replacements: there are those ahead of the bier and those behind it. Those ahead of the bier, who are still needed, are exempt. Those behind the bier, even if still needed, are obligated. Both groups are exempt from תפלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues and tells us which of the people carrying the מטה are exempt from קריאת שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pallbearers take turns. Those 'ahead of the bier' have not carried yet and are still busy with the מצוה, so they are exempt. Those 'behind the bier' already did their turn, so they must say שמע. Everyone is exempt from תפלה, which needs more focus.

keyTerms.meaning: Their replacements, the next shift of carriers

steps.confusionAlert: 'Ahead of' and 'behind' are not really about where people stand. 'Ahead' means those whose turn is still coming. 'Behind' means those who already took their turn.

phrases.english: The bier carriers and their replacements,
and the replacements of their replacements,
those ahead of the bier,
phrases.notes: These are the carriers who haven't had their turn yet.

phrases.english: and those after the bier.

phrases.aramaic: אֶת שֶׁלִּפְנֵי הַמִּטָּה צוֹרֶךְ בָּהֶם — פְּטוּרִין,
phrases.english: Those ahead of the bier, who are needed, are exempt,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶת שֶׁלְּאַחַר הַמִּטָּה צוֹרֶךְ בָּהֶם — חַיָּיבִין.
phrases.english: and those after the bier, even if needed, are obligated.
And both these and those are exempt from prayer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the exemption from the mourner himself to the people carrying the bier.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Carriers still waiting for their turn are exempt from שמע. Those who already carried are obligated. All of them are exempt from תפלה.

steps.title: Returning from the burial: start שמע only if you can finish
steps.stepSummary: After the burial, people begin שמע only if they can finish before reaching the comforters' row.
steps.simpleTranslation: They buried the dead and came back. If they can begin and finish before they reach the row, they should begin. If not, they should not begin.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells the people coming back from the burial when they should start קריאת שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the burial is done, the duty of שמע returns. But soon they will stand in the row to comfort the mourners. So they should start only if they can finish the whole שמע before they get there.

keyTerms.meaning: The row of people who stand to comfort the mourners after the burial

phrases.english: They buried the dead and returned,
if they are able to begin and finish
before they reach the row, they should begin.
phrases.notes: The row is where people line up so the mourners can pass by and be comforted.

phrases.english: And if not, they should not begin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next stage of the funeral, after the burial.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Begin שמע only if there is time to finish before reaching the comforters' row.

steps.title: The comforters' row: inner row exempt, outer row obligated
steps.stepSummary: People in the inner row, who actually comfort the mourners, are exempt. People in the outer row are obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: Those standing in the row: the inner ones are exempt, and the outer ones are obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells us which people standing in the comforters' row must say שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inner row faces the mourners and actually comforts them, so they are busy with a מצוה and exempt. The outer row only stands there out of respect, so they must still say שמע.

keyTerms.meaning: The inner ones, who face the mourners

phrases.english: Those standing in the row,
the inner ones are exempt,
and the outer ones are obligated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the funeral sequence to the row of comforters.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Inner row is exempt from שמע. Outer row is obligated.
steps.whatToRemember: Across the whole funeral, the rule is the same: whoever is actively busy with the dead or the mourners right now is exempt. Whoever is not busy right now is obligated.

steps.title: Women, slaves, and minors: which מצוות apply to them
steps.stepSummary: נשים, עבדים, and קטנים are exempt from קריאת שמע and תפילין. They are obligated in תפלה, מזוזה, and ברכת המזון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Women, slaves, and minors are exempt from קריאת שמע and from תפילין. They are obligated in prayer, מזוזה, and ברכת המזון.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה switches to a new topic: people who are exempt because of who they are, not because they are busy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, every exemption came from being busy with a מצוה. Here the משנה lists people whose status exempts them from some מצוות. It also lists the מצוות they still must do.

keyTerms.meaning: Minors, children below בר מצוה age

phrases.english: Women, slaves, and minors
are exempt from the reading of Shema and from tefillin,
and are obligated in prayer, mezuzah, and grace after meals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the funeral cases and opens a separate list of exemptions based on personal status.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נשים, עבדים, and קטנים are exempt from שמע and תפילין, but obligated in תפלה, מזוזה, and ברכת המזון.
steps.whyThisMatters: This line is a main source for which מצוות נשים are obligated in. The גמרא will later look at it closely.

steps.title: Exempt only when the body is actually lying before him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the משנה's words 'lying before him' closely. The exemption applies when the body is right there, not when it is somewhere else.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: When the body is lying before him, yes, he is exempt. When it is not lying before him, no, he is not exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by pulling an inference out of the opening words of the משנה. This sets up the discussion that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said 'his dead is lying before him.' The גמרא reads this precisely: the exemption depends on the body being physically in front of him. If the body is in another place, he would seem to be obligated. The גמרא is preparing to test this inference against another source.

keyTerms.meaning: Lying before him (the body is right in front of him)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the final הלכה. It is only a first inference from the wording, and the גמרא is about to examine it.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Lying before him, yes,
but when it is not lying before him, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: מוּטָּל לְפָנָיו — אִין, וְשֶׁאֵינוֹ מוּטָּל לְפָנָיו — לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the opening line of the משנה (step 17) and draws an inference from its wording.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Based on the wording, the exemption applies only when the body is physically in front of the mourner.

steps.title: A ברייתא suggests the mourner is exempt even when he is in another room
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא. It describes a mourner who eats away from the body, in another room, a friend's house, or behind a partition. It still says he does not make a ברכה or a זימון. This clashes with the previous step, which said the exemption applies only when the body is right in front of him.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised a contradiction: someone whose dead relative is lying before him eats in another room. If he has no other room, he eats in his friend's house. If he has no friend's house, he makes a partition and eats. If he has nothing to make a partition with, he turns his face away and eats. He does not recline while eating. He does not eat meat or drink wine. He does not make a ברכה, and he does not make a זימון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the previous step. It quotes a ברייתא in which a mourner eats away from the body and is still exempt from ברכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 22 said the exemption depends on the body being physically in front of the mourner. This ברייתא calls him 'one whose dead is lying before him' even while he eats in another room or a friend's house, and it still says 'he does not make a ברכה, and he does not make a זימון.' So it looks like the exemption follows him wherever he is, not only when the body is in the same room.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And they threw them together.' This introduces a source that contradicts what was just said.
Reclining while eating, the way people sat at a festive meal
Leads a זימון, the group invitation to ברכת המזון

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא uses the same words as the משנה, 'lying before him,' yet it describes a man who is in a different room. That is exactly the problem. Do not assume 'before him' must mean physically in front of him. The גמרא is pointing out that this ברייתא seems to use the phrase more broadly.
steps.whyThisMatters: This contradiction makes the גמרא define more carefully when a mourner counts as 'having his dead before him.' That definition decides when he is free from מצוות.

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction: one whose dead relative is lying before him
eats in another room,
and if he does not have another room,
he eats in his friend's house,
and if he does not have a friend's house,
he makes a partition and eats,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם אֵין לוֹ דָּבָר לַעֲשׂוֹת מְחִיצָּה —
phrases.english: and if he has nothing with which to make a partition,
he turns his face away and eats.
And he does not recline while he eats.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵינוֹ אוֹכֵל בָּשָׂר וְאֵינוֹ שׁוֹתֶה יַיִן,
phrases.english: And he does not eat meat and does not drink wine,
and he does not make a blessing, and he does not make a zimmun.
phrases.notes: This is the punchline. Even in another room, he is still exempt from ברכות, and that is what clashes with step 22.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 22's close reading, which limited the exemption to when the body is physically in front of the mourner.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 22 that the exemption applies only when the body is right in front of the mourner, and not when it is elsewhere.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא has the mourner eating in another room or a friend's house, away from the body. It still exempts him from ברכה and זימון. So the exemption seems to apply even when the body is not physically before him.
